title: A Sparsity-Aware Distributed-Memory Algorithm for Sparse-Sparse Matrix Multiplication
problem: Existing distributed-memory sparse matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) algorithms use sparsity-oblivious 2D and 3D partitioning that fetch all nonzeros regardless of whether they participate in the multiplication. This results in unnecessary communication overhead in distributed systems.
motivation: SpGEMM is a critical computational primitive in graph algorithms, bioinformatics, algebraic multigrid solvers, and randomized sketching, requiring efficient distributed implementations for large-scale scientific computing.
method: The algorithm identifies which numbers in the sparse matrices actually participate in the multiplication, then fetches only those from other computers instead of everything. It uses 1D partitioning (splitting data along one dimension) rather than the typical two-dimensional or three-dimensional approaches to determine participation. When transferring data between computers, it employs MPI RDMA (direct memory-to-memory transfer that bypasses packing overhead) and groups small requests into larger blocks to reduce the number of individual messages. The approach is tested against CombBLAS 2D and 3D implementations across various configurations.
key_novelty: The algorithm uses 1D partitioning with sparsity-awareness to fetch only numbers contributing to the multiplication, employing direct memory transfers (MPI RDMA) and batched requests instead of standard multi-dimensional partitioning.
contributions: Sparsity-aware 1D distributed-memory SpGEMM algorithm that theoretically reduces communication versus sparsity-oblivious 2D/3D approaches
MPI RDMA-based implementation with block fetching strategy to mitigate packing/unpacking overhead and fine-grained messaging
Empirical demonstration that 1D implementation outperforms state-of-the-art CombBLAS 2D/3D implementations across multiple configurations and use cases
Simpler conceptual design compared to existing distributed SpGEMM algorithms
